§3§lPreparation and quest§r
The Device Info Terminal manages supported GT machines in an EU ledger. This quest detects §11§r terminal and §2does not consume it§r. The crafting-table recipe uses §12§r LV Sensors, §12§r LV Emitters, §13§r Steel Plates, §11§r Computer Screen Cover and §11§r Ender Pearl.

§3§lBinding, viewing and names§r
With visualization off, right-click a supported machine to bind it; supported machines placed while carrying the terminal also bind automatically. Right-click air to open the list. Rows show Running, Idle or Stopped status, actual EU input/output, instantaneous and average EU/t, position and available recipe previews. Consumption is negative; direct GT wireless-grid transactions are also measured, and icons identify this mod's input/output link nodes. Hover the name for a readable recipe, or enable Show Recipe in the list. Name, Status, Instantaneous, Average and Position can be sorted; choose Normal, Scientific, metric K/M/G/T/P or GT voltage-tier formatting. Alt-left-click a machine name to rename it, select a color and toggle bold; Ctrl-click a row unbinds it remotely.

§3§lSampling and ignored machines§r
Sampling defaults to once every §110 seconds§r; instantaneous EU/t uses the latest observation of the recent §120-tick§r flow window, and averages use §160§r rolling points. Shift-right-click a machine, or Shift-click its list row, toggles tracking/ignored only for this terminal. For an unbound machine it records the preference without binding. Passive energy storage and transformers default to ignored. Ignored entries stay gray with zero readings and are not tracked; this preference does not switch the machine itself off.

§3§lCharged scan§r
Hold Alt+right-click for about §11 second§r, including while aiming at a block. Charge completion immediately starts a scan of your and your team's machines in loaded chunks of the current dimension; repeating the charge does not cancel an active scan. Ordinary scans skip ignored machines. Charge again with the same terminal within §115 seconds§r after completion to force them into the list, keeping their ignored status and gray zero readings. The default binding limit is §11024§r; scans do not load chunks.

§3§lPersistent visualization and settings§r
Shift+Alt+right-click toggles and saves visualization. The enabled terminal gains an enchantment glint; its bound-machine anchors remain visible while it is in inventory. Labels can independently show names, status, live EU input/output and recipes. Shift-right-click air or a non-machine opens settings for range, opacity, occlusion, device/label limits and other display options. Energy heat uses warm red for consumption and green for generation, with smooth radii weighted from instantaneous and average load. Heat size ranges from §11–1000§r, default §110§r (ten times the original radius limit); label size ranges from §11–100§r, default §110§r (150 percent of the original).

§3§lTeleportation and server settings§r
Hold this terminal with visualization enabled and ordinary right-click while aiming at its bound machine or marker to teleport; when no bound target is aimed at, the list opens. The row teleport button provides the same travel action. Default cost is §11 XP level§r and cooldown §110 ticks (0.5 seconds)§r. A loaded, valid destination is required: the nearest safe position in front of or above the controller is chosen, and flying players may use clear air without ground support. XP is charged only after successful teleportation. Existing configuration is retained; singleplayer changes save to the local instance, and multiplayer OP changes on the Server tab persist to server configuration and synchronize online players. Set the XP cost to §10§r for free travel; keep client and server versions aligned.
